pages.text: "Yum, gulp!" Bami stuffed lunch into their beak in the dining car. Pipi called, "Next station soon!" "I'll eat quickly, then wave the flag!" A yellow flag stood nearby.
Bami took a huge bite of boiled potato and swallowed without chewing. Bite, gulp, bite, gulp! "I need to welcome passengers!" Their beak was packed full.
Suddenly—"Hic! Hic!" Hiccups came and their throat felt tight. The hiccups wouldn't stop; Bami's eyes filled with tears. The train squealed into the station.
Dad, the engine driver, came from the cab, gently stroked Bami's back, and offered water. "Slowly. A sip." The hiccups settled. "You swallowed too fast." Dad sat beside Bami.
A rabbit family boarded with a big basket. Across the aisle, three children crunched carrots. Dad whispered, "They chew each bite ten times. Their tummies never hurt." Bami counted. Really—ten!
"Let's play the ten-chew game. A little bite, ten chews, then swallow!" Dad said. "Chew well, take your time!" The three rabbits hopped. "We'll count with you!" Bami's eyes sparkled.
Bami took a little potato. The rabbits counted each chew. "One, two, three... ten!" Sweet flavor spread. "Was it always this good? Chew well, take your time!"
A slow meal left Bami's tummy comfortable, with no hiccups or throat trouble. Dad returned to the cab. Bami held the flag in a foot by the door and waved with wings wide. Ding! "Departure!"

Now Bami knew the steps. "One, a little bite! Two, ten chews! Three, swallow when it's chewed!" Next day, even when Pipi called the next station, Bami chewed ten times. Flowers covered spring hills outside.
Dad hugged Bami. "A fine conductor who chews well!" Slow chewing made lunch tastier and their tummy comfortable. Chew well, take your time!
